spec_points.text: 1.1.1 The purpose and nature of business activity:
sub_items: Concepts of needs, wants, scarcity and opportunity cost
Importance of specialisation
Purpose of business activity
The concept of adding value and how added value can be increased

spec_points.text: 1.2.1 Economic sectors in terms of primary, secondary and tertiary sectors:
sub_items: Basis of business classification, using examples to illustrate the classification
Reasons for the changing importance of business classification, e.g. in developed and developing economies

spec_points.text: Classify business enterprises between private
1.3.1 Enterprise and entrepreneurship:
sub_items: Characteristics of successful entrepreneurs
Contents of a business plan and how business plans assist entrepreneurs
Why and how governments support business start-ups, e.g. grants, training schemes

spec_points.text: 1.3.2 The methods and problems of measuring business size:
sub_items: Methods of measuring business size, e.g. number of people employed, value of output, capital employed (profit is not a method of measuring business size)
Limitations of methods of measuring business size

spec_points.text: 1.3.3 Why some businesses grow and others remain small:

subsection.title: Enterprise, business growth and size continued

sub_items: Why the owners of a business may want to expand the business
Different ways in which businesses can grow, e.g. internal/external
Problems linked to business growth and how these might be overcome
Why some businesses remain small

spec_points.text: 1.3.4 Why some (new or established) businesses fail:

subsection.title: Enterprise, business growth and size continued

sub_items: Causes of business failure, e.g. lack of management skills, changes in the business environment, liquidity problems
Why new businesses are at a greater risk of failing

spec_points.text: 1.4.1 The main features of different forms of business organisation:
sub_items: Sole traders, partnerships, private and public limited companies, franchises and joint ventures
Differences between unincorporated businesses and limited companies
Concepts of risk, ownership and limited liability
Recommend and justify a suitable form of business organisation to owners/management in a given situation
Business organisations in the public sector, e.g. public corporations

spec_points.text: 1.5.1 Businesses can have several objectives and the importance of them can change:
sub_items: Need for business objectives and the importance of them
Different business objectives, e.g. survival, growth, profit and market share
Objectives of social enterprises

spec_points.text: 1.5.2 The role of stakeholder groups involved in business activity:
sub_items: Main internal and external stakeholder groups
Objectives of different stakeholder groups
How these objectives might conflict with each other, use examples

spec_points.text: Differences in the objectives of private sector
2.1.1 The importance of a well-motivated workforce:
sub_items: Why people work and what motivation means
The benefits of a well-motivated workforce: labour productivity, reduced absenteeism and labour turnover
The concept of human needs, e.g. Maslow’s hierarchy
Key motivational theories: Taylor and Herzberg

spec_points.text: 2.1.2 Methods of motivation:
sub_items: Financial rewards, e.g. wage, salary, bonus, commission and profit sharing
Non-financial methods, e.g. job enrichment, job rotation, teamworking, training, opportunities for promotion
Recommend and justify appropriate method(s) of motivation in given circumstances

spec_points.text: 2.2.1 Draw, interpret and understand simple organisational charts:
sub_items: Simple hierarchical structures: levels of hierarchy, span of control, chain of command e.g. tall/short
Roles and responsibilities of directors, managers, supervisors, other employees in an organisation and inter-relationships between them

spec_points.text: 2.2.2 The role of management:
sub_items: Functions of management, e.g. planning, organising, coordinating, commanding and controlling
Importance of delegation; trust versus control

spec_points.text: 2.2.3 Leadership styles:
sub_items: Features of the main leadership styles, e.g. autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire
Recommend and justify an appropriate leadership style in given circumstances

spec_points.text: 2.2.4 Trade unions:
sub_items: What a trade union is and the effects of employees being union members

spec_points.text: 2.3.1 Recruitment and selecting employees:

subsection.title: Recruitment, selection and training of employees

sub_items: Recruitment and selection methods
Difference between internal recruitment and external recruitment
Main stages in recruitment and selection of employees
Recommend and justify who to employ in given circumstances
Benefits and limitations of part-time employees and full-time employees

spec_points.text: 2.3.2 The importance of training and the methods of training:

subsection.title: Recruitment, selection and training of employees

sub_items: Importance of training to a business and to employees
Benefits and limitations of induction training, on-the-job training and off-the-job training

spec_points.text: 2.3.3 Why reducing the size of the workforce might be necessary:

subsection.title: Recruitment, selection and training of employees

sub_items: Difference between dismissal and redundancy with examples
Understand situations in which downsizing the workforce might be necessary, e.g. automation or reduced demand for products
Recommend and justify which employees to make redundant in given circumstances

spec_points.text: 2.3.4 Legal controls over employment issues and their impact on employers and employees:

subsection.title: Recruitment, selection and training of employees

sub_items: Legal controls over employment contracts, unfair dismissal, discrimination, health and safety, legal minimum wage

spec_points.text: 2.4.1 Why effective communication is important and the methods used to achieve it:
sub_items: Effective communication and its importance to business
Benefits and limitations of different communication methods including those based on information technology (IT)
Recommend and justify which communication method to use in given circumstances

spec_points.text: 2.4.2 Demonstrate an awareness of communication barriers:
sub_items: How communication barriers arise and problems of ineffective communication; how communication barriers can be reduced or removed

spec_points.text: 3.1.1 The role of marketing:
sub_items: Identifying customer needs
Satisfying customer needs
Maintaining customer loyalty
Building customer relationships

spec_points.text: 3.1.2 Market changes:
sub_items: Why customer/consumer spending patterns may change
The importance of changing customer needs
Why some markets have become more competitive
How businesses can respond to changing spending patterns and increased competition

spec_points.text: 3.1.3 Concepts of niche marketing and mass marketing:
sub_items: Benefits and limitations of both approaches to marketing

spec_points.text: 3.1.4 How and why market segmentation is undertaken:
sub_items: How markets can be segmented, e.g. according to age, socio-economic grouping, location, gender
Potential benefits of segmentation to business
Recommend and justify an appropriate method of segmentation in given circumstances

spec_points.text: 3.2.1 The role of market research and methods used:
sub_items: Market-orientated businesses (uses of market research information to a business)
Primary research and secondary research (benefits and limitations of each)
Methods of primary research, e.g. postal questionnaire, online survey, interviews, focus groups
The need for sampling
Methods of secondary research, e.g. online, accessing government sources, paying for commercial market research reports
Factors influencing the accuracy of market research data

spec_points.text: 3.2.2 Presentation and use of market research results:
sub_items: Analyse market research data shown in the form of graphs, charts and diagrams; draw simple conclusions from such data

spec_points.text: 3.3.1 Product:
sub_items: The limitations and benefits of developing new products
Brand image; impact on sales and customer loyalty
The role of packaging
The product life cycle: main stages and extension strategies; draw and interpret a product life cycle diagram
How stages of the product life cycle can influence marketing decisions, e.g. promotion and pricing decisions

spec_points.text: 3.3.2 Price:
sub_items: Pricing methods (benefits and limitations of different methods), e.g. cost plus, competitive, penetration, skimming, and promotional
Recommend and justify an appropriate pricing method in given circumstances

Understand the significance of price elasticity: difference between price elastic demand and price inelastic demand; importance of the concept in pricing decisions (knowledge of the formula and calculations of PED will not be assessed)

spec_points.text: 3.3.3 Place – distribution channels:
sub_items: Advantages and disadvantages of different channels, e.g. use of wholesalers, retailers or direct to consumers
Recommend and justify an appropriate distribution channel in given circumstances

spec_points.text: 3.3.4 Promotion:
sub_items: The aims of promotion
Different forms of promotion and how they influence sales, e.g. advertising, sales promotion
The need for cost-effectiveness in spending the marketing budget on promotion

spec_points.text: 3.3.5 Technology and the marketing mix:
sub_items: Define and explain the concept of e-commerce
The opportunities and threats of e-commerce to business and consumers
Use of the internet and social media networks for promotion

spec_points.text: 3.4.1 Justify marketing strategies appropriate to a given situation:
sub_items: Importance of different elements of the marketing mix in influencing consumer decisions in given circumstances
Recommend and justify an appropriate marketing strategy in given circumstances

spec_points.text: 3.4.2 The nature and impact of legal controls related to marketing:
sub_items: Impact of legal controls on marketing strategy, e.g. misleading promotion, faulty and dangerous goods

spec_points.text: 3.4.3 The opportunities and problems of entering new foreign markets:
sub_items: Growth potential of new markets in other countries
Problems of entering foreign markets, e.g. cultural differences and lack of knowledge
Benefits and limitations of methods to overcome such problems, e.g. joint ventures, licensing

spec_points.text: 4.1.1 The meaning of production:
sub_items: Managing resources effectively to produce goods and services
Difference between production and productivity
Benefits of increasing efficiency and how to increase it, e.g. increasing productivity by automation and technology, improved labour skills
Why businesses hold inventories
The concept of lean production: how to achieve it, e.g. just-in-time inventory control and Kaizen; benefits of lean production

spec_points.text: 4.1.2 The main methods of production:
sub_items: Features, benefits and limitations of job, batch and flow production
Recommend and justify an appropriate production method for a given situation

spec_points.text: How technology has changed and is changing
4.2.1 Identify and classify costs:

subsection.title: Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis

sub_items: Classifying costs using examples, e.g. fixed, variable, average, total
Use cost data to help make simple cost-based decisions, e.g. to stop production or continue

spec_points.text: 4.2.2 Economies and diseconomies of scale:

subsection.title: Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis

sub_items: The concept of economies of scale with examples, e.g. purchasing, marketing, financial, managerial, technical
The concept of diseconomies of scale with examples, e.g. poor communication, lack of commitment from employees, weak coordination

spec_points.text: 4.2.3 Break-even analysis:

subsection.title: Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis

sub_items: The concept of break-even
Construct, complete or amend a simple break-even chart
Interpret a given chart and use it to analyse a situation
Calculate break-even output from given data
Define, calculate and interpret the margin of safety
Use break-even analysis to help make simple decisions, e.g. impact of higher price
Understand the limitations of break-even analysis

spec_points.text: 4.3.1 Why quality is important and how quality production might be achieved:
sub_items: What quality means and why it is important for all businesses
The concept of quality control and how businesses implement quality control
The concept of quality assurance and how this can be implemented

spec_points.text: 4.4.1 The main factors influencing the location and relocation decisions of a business:
sub_items: Factors relevant to the location decision of manufacturing businesses and service businesses
Factors that a business could consider when deciding which country to locate operations in
The role of legal controls on location decisions
Recommend and justify an appropriate location for a business in given circumstances

spec_points.text: 5.1.1 The need for business finance:
sub_items: The main reasons why businesses need finance, e.g. start-up capital, capital for expansion and additional working capital
Understand the difference between short-term and long-term finance needs

spec_points.text: 5.1.2 The main sources of finance:
sub_items: Internal sources and external sources with examples
Short-term and long-term sources with examples, e.g. overdraft for short-term finance and debt or equity for long-term finance
Importance of alternative sources of capital, e.g. micro-finance, crowd-funding
The main factors considered in making the financial choice, e.g. size and legal form of business, amount required, length of time, existing loans
Recommend and justify appropriate source(s) of finance in given circumstances

spec_points.text: 5.2.1 The importance of cash and of cash-flow forecasting:
sub_items: Why cash is important to a business
What a cash-flow forecast is, how a simple one is constructed and the importance of it
Amend or complete a simple cash-flow forecast
How to interpret a simple cash-flow forecast
How a short-term cash-flow problem might be overcome, e.g. overdraft, delaying supplier payments, asking debtors to pay more quickly

spec_points.text: 5.2.2 Working capital:
sub_items: The concept and importance of working capital

spec_points.text: 5.3.1 What profit is and why it is important:
sub_items: How a profit is made
Importance of profit to private sector businesses, e.g. reward for risk-taking/enterprise, source of finance
Difference between profit and cash

spec_points.text: 5.3.2 Income statements:
sub_items: Main features of an income statement, e.g. revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, profit and retained profit
Use simple income statements in decision- making based on profit calculations (constructing income statements will not be assessed)

spec_points.text: 5.4.1 The main elements of a statement of financial position:
sub_items: The main classifications of assets and liabilities, using examples

spec_points.text: Interpret a simple statement of financial
5.5.1 Profitability:
sub_items: The concept and importance of profitability

spec_points.text: 5.5.2 Liquidity:
sub_items: The concept and importance of liquidity

spec_points.text: 5.5.3 How to interpret the financial performance of a business by calculating and analysing profitability ratios and liquidity ratios:
sub_items: Gross profit margin
Profit margin
Return on Capital Employed
Current ratio
Acid test ratio

spec_points.text: 5.5.4 Why and how accounts are used:
sub_items: Needs of different users of accounts and ratio analysis
How users of accounts and ratio results might use information to help make decisions, e.g. whether to lend to or invest in the business

spec_points.text: 6.1.1 Business cycle:
sub_items: Main stages of the business cycle, e.g. growth, boom, recession, slump
Impact on businesses of changes in employment levels, inflation and Gross Domestic Product (GDP)

spec_points.text: 6.1.2 How government control over the economy affects business activity and how businesses may respond:
sub_items: Identify government economic objectives, e.g. increasing Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
Impact of changes in taxes and government spending
Impact of changes in interest rates
How businesses might respond to these changes

spec_points.text: 6.2.1 Environmental concerns and ethical issues as both opportunities and constraints for businesses:
sub_items: How business activity can impact on the environment, e.g. global warming
The concept of externalities: possible external costs and external benefits of business decisions
Sustainable development; how business activity can contribute to this
How and why business might respond to environmental pressures and opportunities, e.g. pressure groups
The role of legal controls over business activity affecting the environment, e.g. pollution controls
Ethical issues a business might face: conflicts between profits and ethics
How business might react and respond to ethical issues, e.g. child labour, paying fair prices to suppliers

spec_points.text: 6.3.1 The importance of globalisation:
sub_items: The concept of globalisation and the reasons for it
Opportunities and threats of globalisation for businesses
Why governments might introduce import tariffs and import quotas

spec_points.text: 6.3.2 Reasons for the importance and growth of multinational companies (MNCs):

subsection.title: Business and the international economy continued

sub_items: Benefits to a business of becoming a multinational and the impact on its stakeholders
Potential benefits to a country and/or economy where a MNC is located, e.g. jobs, exports, increased choice, investment
Potential drawbacks to a country and/or economy where a MNC is located, e.g. reduced sales of local businesses, repatriation of profits

spec_points.text: 6.3.3 The impact of exchange rate changes:

subsection.title: Business and the international economy continued

sub_items: Depreciation and appreciation of an exchange rate
How exchange rate changes can affect businesses as importers and exporters of products, e.g. prices, competitiveness, profitability (exchange rate calculations will not be assessed)
